feature_under_test: same-node MySQL process death, crash recovery, and result resumption while a real-Chrome request is in flight

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root staircase_migrator and staircase_runtime accounts
environment.database_storage: test-only restartable Docker data volume removed during cleanup
environment.stable_runtime_endpoint: test-process transparent TCP proxy retargeted to the restarted container's published port

fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: block the stable runtime endpoint, SIGKILL the MySQL container, hold the process down for seven seconds, restart the same container and data, retarget the proxy, then resume forwarding

fixture_calibration.finding: Docker reallocated a random published host port when the same container restarted, so the old test DSN remained connection-refused even though MySQL crash recovery completed and the container was healthy
fixture_calibration.correction: keep the runtime DSN pointed at a stable transparent proxy and retarget only the proxy upstream after restart; no production configuration or code changed

invariants: MySQL receives SIGKILL only after the Attempt is running, the request reached the origin, and no Artifact exists
Server and execution daemon remain alive while the database process is absent and performs crash recovery
the same database retains the seeded Work, Attempt, Recipe, Job, receipt, and outbox facts across process death
the Executor resends the immutable result through its bounded control retry path instead of rerunning the Recipe
the original Attempt succeeds without a replacement Attempt, recovery dispatch, or second website request
one DOM response, one effect trace, and one BackfillOutput commit after database recovery
all Permits and dispatches settle, and a final Server restart preserves state and both Resource reads

implementation.reused_production_behavior: bounded immutable result replay introduced by BF4 in drivers/tools/recruitingexecutor/control_client.go; no production edit required for BF5

non_claims: point-in-time recovery, corrupted storage, data loss, or a different database node
remote-network behavior or a long outage beyond control_wait_ms
simultaneous Atoll Server and MySQL failure

acceptance.gate: P9 MySQL process death during an in-flight real-Chrome request
